_comment: The pre-commit BUILD GATE: the single highest-leverage hook. Before any `git commit`,
run your stack's cheapest 'does it still compile / collect' command. If it fails, the
commit is denied with the reason, and the agent fixes the build before landing it.
Drop this block into .claude/settings.json under hooks.PreToolUse (or use
templates/settings.json.template, which wires this plus the two guards).
Pick ONE command for your stack and put it where `<build-command>` is:
Next.js:      npx next build --no-lint
TypeScript:   npx tsc --noEmit
Rust:         cargo check
Go:           go build ./...
Python:       python -m pytest --collect-only -q
.NET:         dotnet build --no-restore
Notes:
- `if: Bash(git commit:*)` scopes the hook to commits only; add/push/status pass untouched.
- `cd "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"` keeps the gate on the repo the session opened, so a
compound `cd elsewhere && git commit` still builds the right tree.
- Keep the timeout honest. A gate that times out reads as a failure; if your build
takes 5 minutes, use a cheaper check (tsc --noEmit, pytest --collect-only).
- Run it the way CI runs it. CI often sets CI=true, which turns warnings into errors.
- On Windows the same command works from Git Bash. From PowerShell use
`Set-Location $env:CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR; <build-command>` and `"shell": "powershell"`.

hooks.command: cd "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR" && <build-command> > /dev/null 2>&1 || echo '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"Build failed. Fix the build before committing."}}'
